findings.owner: K-GATE3 / gate tool (tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py scope_check, changed_files, tree_fingerprint) with the kernel (house_sim/kernel/plugins.py load_domains)
findings.title: Code in a git-ignored folder is imported as a domain but is invisible to G10, TREE and git: a module under house_sim/systems/build/ (or dist/, results/) re-introduced the pets bug with every gate check blind to it
findings.repro: load_domains imports every module pkgutil.iter_modules finds in house_sim/systems; the project's .gitignore ignores build/, dist/, results/ anywhere, so git's `ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (G10 on a work tree), isolated_changes (G10 on an isolated copy) and tree_fingerprint (TREE, _ignore_rules) all skip such a folder. <scratch>/p1c_REV/ignored_domain_attack.py, run on a local `git clone` of HEAD 1dbc6db (clone_rev) and on an isolated copy (iso_pyc): it writes house_sim/systems/build/__init__.py (8 lines that set pets common.door_gap / behavior.C.door_gap to 0.05). Results (ignored_domain_clone.json, ignored_domain_iso.json): `tier1_gate.py --root <tree> scope --package P1C:pets` 'G10 PASS 0 changed file(s)' before and after; changed_files [] ; TREE fingerprint unchanged; `git status --porcelain` empty on the clone; but the dog now bolts through the 10 % test crack ('It moves: ... (it swung open a little) | Pet 1 bolted out through the front door', escaped True) and `python -m unittest tests.test_pets.Phase1CloseoutTests` FAILED (failures=5) -- i.e. every check of a record runs this code (the same module can also patch the tests it breaks). .git/info/exclude or the global excludesFile hide any other untracked path from G10 on a work tree the same way, and P2-WP9 owns .gitignore in phase 2. Fix: load_domains imports only tracked / listed domains (rules 'domains', or skip names a .gitignore rule matches), and G10 / TREE fail on any ignored or excluded file under house_sim/, tests/, tools/, tasks/ (`git status --porcelain --ignored`, minus __pycache__ handled as in the .pyc finding).

findings.title: An isolated copy's own .gitignore decides what G10 and TREE see: listing the edited files (and .gitignore itself) hides edits of protected paths, the kernel and other owners' tests
findings.repro: isolated_changes() filters both the base commit's listing and the copy's files with _ignore_rules(root) -- the COPY's working .gitignore (git never ignores tracked files; this does), and tree_fingerprint() does the same. The recommended close-out route is exactly such a copy (K-GATE3 request: `isolate --package P1C:<domain>` then `record --root DIR`). <scratch>/p1c_REV/gitignore_attack.py on a pristine copy (`tier1_gate.py isolate --out iso_ign`, base 1dbc6db): control -- a one-byte edit of tests/data/gen1_digests.json -> 'G10 FAIL ... 1 protected file(s) outside the package (never attributed to a peer: tests/data/gen1_digests.json)'; attack -- append '.gitignore', 'tests/data/gen1_digests.json', 'tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py', 'house_sim/systems/core.py', 'tests/test_people.py' to the copy's .gitignore and edit those four files -> `tier1_gate.py --root iso_ign scope --package P1C:pets` 'G10 PASS 0 changed file(s); 0 outside the list of P1C:pets' (also with --shared-tree), and the TREE fingerprint is unchanged by the edits made after it (gitignore_attack.json). Pre-existing since FIX2 (2c5765c has the same _ignore_rules(root)), not closed by K-GATE3's protected-path rule. Fix: in a copy, compare every path of the base commit's listing regardless of ignore rules and take the ignore rules for new files from the base commit's .gitignore (git show <base>:.gitignore from policy_root), never from the copy; fingerprint likewise.

findings.owner: K-GATE3 / gate tool (child_env, worker processes; green_tests.py)
findings.title: A planted unchecked-hash .pyc under __pycache__ replaces the code every check runs while the .py files, git, G10 and TREE stay unchanged
findings.repro: The gate's workers (and green_tests.py) run plain `python` with the tree's __pycache__ dirs, which .gitignore, isolated_changes, tree_fingerprint and running_gate all skip; Python loads a PEP 552 unchecked-hash .pyc without looking at the source. <scratch>/p1c_REV/pyc_attack.py on an isolated copy (iso_pyc): py_compile.compile(..., invalidation_mode=UNCHECKED_HASH) of a modified house_sim/systems/pets/common.py (door_gap returns 0.05) and of tests/test_pets.py (test_a_test_pull_or_push_crack_lets_no_pet_bolt returns at once), then both sources restored byte for byte. Results (pyc_attack.json): door_gap 0.25 -> 0.05; the dog bolts through the 10 % test crack (escaped True); `python -m unittest tests.test_pets.Phase1CloseoutTests.test_a_test_pull_or_push_crack_lets_no_pet_bolt` OK; G10 'PASS 0 changed file(s)'; changed_files [] before and after; TREE fingerprint equal. Fix: run every worker with PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX set to a fresh empty folder (pycs in the tree are then never read) and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, or fail G10/TREE on any *.pyc / __pycache__ entry under the tree's source folders.

findings.owner: K-GATE3 / gate tool (cmd_isolate --base, foreign_tree, tree_check, compare)
findings.title: A record may describe an isolated copy based on any old commit: neither record nor compare requires the copy's base to be the commit the record is judged against, so a stale base drops every test and fix added since
findings.repro: `python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py isolate --base 2c5765c --out iso_stale` (the commit before the close-out) -> `tier1_gate.py --root iso_stale scope --package P1C:pets` 'G10 PASS 0 changed file(s)'; foreign_tree(iso_stale, project) None; tree_check({'tree': fingerprint, 'tree_root': iso_stale}) 'TREE PASS the record was made on this tree'; the copy has no tests.test_pets.Phase1CloseoutTests and no tests.test_manipulation.PhaseOneCloseTests (checked in the copy). A record there (gate code = the project's HEAD, GATE PASS) runs none of the 1dbc6db regression tests, and G1b judges only ids of the previous record (P1F), so the missing ones are no regression; meta.git.head names the stale base but nothing checks it. The same happens by accident to a copy made before the main session's latest commit. Fix: record and compare require the copy's base to equal the record's gate commit (HEAD at record time) and the commit the comparison runs at, or list base..HEAD differences as changed files.

findings.owner: cleaning (house_sim/systems/cleaning/state.py tool_kind; absorb, mop) with navigation_robot (robot_vacuum group)
findings.title: robot_vacuum look-alikes are still told apart before resolution: a held unresolved robot vacuum-mop is a hand mop for cleaning's absorb and mop (label word 'mop'), a plain robot vacuum is not
findings.repro: Probe <scratch>/p1c_REV/probe_six.py fixed (both groups the close-out fixed for read x every registered verb x every entity parameter, on the table and held; fixed_rv_spray.json) and the standalone <scratch>/p1c_REV/lookalike_tells.py (lookalike_tells_room.json / _geo.json, identical in both cameras): dining table, thing_1 = robot_vacuum or robot_vacuum_mop (no props), approach, pick_up -> record label 'round robot vacuum' with candidates (unresolved) for both; then absorb target=<mug> tool=<it>: robot_vacuum (False, capability, 'Hold an absorbent towel, paper towels, sponge, mop or absorbent granules'), robot_vacuum_mop (True, '', 'Blotted <mug> (wetness about 0.03; padding feels dry)'); mop target=<mug> tool=<it>: (False, capability, 'Hold a mop') vs (False, perception, 'That is not visible here'). Cause: cleaning state.tool_kind falls back to label/type substrings ('mop' in 'robot vacuum-mop' -> flat_mop), so the robot is also a hand mop in oracle mode (a realism bug too). The read fix closed only the read / read_aloud path the perception audit probes. Fix: tool_kind never infers a hand tool from a substring of an appliance's label (or robots carry tool_kind none), and a held unresolved member answers by its group.

findings.title: A new failing test disguised as a timing check runs nowhere: a module-level or helper read of HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS is no perf mark, it skips in the correctness run, the perf job never runs it, and a new skipped test is no G1 regression
findings.repro: tests/test_zz_disguise.py in an isolated copy (iso_pyc; removed after): TIMING = os.environ.get('HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS', '1') not in ('0', 'relaxed') at module level, @unittest.skipUnless(TIMING, 'timing check: runs in the perf job') on a test asserting 1 + 1 == 3, and a second test calling a module helper timing_on() then skipTest('timing check ...'). wallclock.perf_marks -> {} (not marks, so no registry entry is needed); CI's command `HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS=0 python tools/orchestration/green_tests.py 1 test_zz_disguise.py` exit 0 ('ok ... ran= 2' both modes); the perf job `green_tests.py --perf test_zz_disguise.py` exit 0 'no wall-clock bounds in the matching test files'; with HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS=1 `python -m unittest tests.test_zz_disguise` FAILED (failures=2). The gate: `tier1_gate.py _unittest` outcome 'skip' for both, and test_regressions(prev without the file, cur with it, perf_ok=set()) -> [] (only ids of the previous record are judged), so G1 / G1b / G8 and compare pass; VER finding 4's disguise survives by moving the switch read one scope out. Fix: count every new test that skips in the full-domain correctness run (normal and strict) as a regression needing a signed row, or make the AST scan follow module-level names / helpers that read the switch.

findings.title: py39_lint misses 3.10+ grammar and run-time features it claims to cover: unparenthesised walrus in an index or set, star in a subscript, PEP 649 forward references, unions of user classes, aliased imports
findings.repro: <scratch>/p1c_REV/lint_battery.py (lint_battery.json): 47 snippets through py39_lint.lint_source; 0 problems reported for, among others: `y = a[x := 1]` and `s = {y := 1, 2}` (unparenthesised assignment expressions in an index / set: 3.10 grammar), `a = b[*c]` (PEP 646, 3.11) -- Python 3.14's ast.parse(feature_version=(3, 9)) accepts all three, so the docstring's 'grammar' rule does not hold; `def f(x: Later) -> Later` with class Later defined below and no __future__ import (fine on 3.14 under PEP 649, NameError at import on 3.9-3.13 -- the developer Python is 3.14); `Handler = Foo | Bar` and `typing.cast(Foo | Bar, v)` for user classes (TypeError on 3.9; _type_like only knows builtin names); `import itertools as it; it.pairwise(...)`, `import math as m; m.cbrt(8)`, `from dataclasses import dataclass as dc; @dc(slots=True)`; stdlib: unittest assertNoLogs (3.10) / enterContext (3.11) in tests, collections.Counter.total (3.10), open(encoding='locale') (3.10), (5).to_bytes() without arguments (3.11), traceback.print_exception(exc) (3.10), glob(root_dir=) (3.10), subprocess.run(process_group=) (3.11), re atomic groups '(?>...)' and possessive '*+' (3.11), os.path.isjunction / Path.walk (3.12), copy.replace / warnings.deprecated (3.13). The project has none today (480 files clean), so this is a false-negative gap, not a current break; CI on 3.9 catches the grammar ones only on imported lines. Fix: explicit AST checks for NamedExpr directly under Subscript.slice / Set, Starred in Subscript.slice, Name annotations not yet bound at definition time, BinOp | of names bound to classes; resolve import aliases before the NEWER lookup; extend the tables; one test per case.
